simple.meaning: פְּרָזָה (pᵉrâzâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “an open country.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פְּרָזָה (H6519) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Esther 9:19, with occurrences in Esther, Ezekiel, Zechariah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פְּרָזָה (H6519) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פְּרָזָה (H6519) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פְּרָזָה (pᵉrâzâh) / H6519 is traced through Esther 9:19, Ezekiel 38:11, Zechariah 2:8 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6519. perazah [ מְּרָזָה ] noun feminine open region, hamlet ; — only plural פ ׳אֶרֶץ ׃מְּרָזוֺת Ezek 38:11 a land of hamlets (opposed to חוֺמָה etc.); ׳פ יְרוּשָׁלַם תֵּשֵׁב Zech 2:8 as open regions shall Jerusalem sit ( יָשַׁב 4 ); הַמּ ׳עָרֵי Est 9:19 (opposed to שׁוּשָׁן 9:18 ); perhaps Judg 5:7 ( ׳פ for מְּרָזוֺן , compare ᵑ7 ᵑ6 GFM).

occurrences.englishText: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a good day, and a day of sending presents of food to one another.
You will say, ‘I will go up to the land of unwalled villages. I will go to those who are at rest, who dwell securely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having neither bars nor gates,
For Yahweh of Armies says: ‘For honor he has sent me to the nations which plundered you; for he who touches you touches the apple of his eye.
